_what: THE PERFUME THREAD -- Nightwish's 'Perfume Of The Timeless' (third-party 4K picture upload O0lyFqLr3Cc) plays from the first frame of the show to the last frame before the credits, with the eight acts living inside it. Movement 1 is the PROLOGUE (scripts/build_prologue.py, source 0 -> 91.200 picture / 99.200 audio). Movements 2-5 are this file: the rest of the same video, IN SOURCE ORDER AND WITHOUT GAPS, seated between the acts. It is not four interstitials -- it is one song the acts interrupt.
_owner: Owner instruction, 2026-08-14: 'Start at ~1:31 or wherever the last cut left off from (check another agent doing parallel work) - save the clip and cut it at ~2.39, then insert that after the destiny intro. 2-39-5:29 is the the next segment, insert after mrbobby. 5:29- start there and record that to 6:30, then insert that before europa. 6:30 match the transition panning up from laura after europa, then hold until the end of this, then roll credits.'
_no_numerals: These take NO ACT NUMERAL and get NO SLIDE and NO CHAPTER MARKER. AGENTS.md makes the eight numerals load-bearing, and the prologue already set the precedent for unnumbered connective tissue in front of act I. A slide announcing an interlude would announce the one thing whose whole job is to be unannounced.
_not_in_prod: They deliver to renders/ ONLY, not to ~/Videos/Wolves/Prod. Owner: 'also want the snippets in the render folder we will be editing them in the future with dino artwork.' They are work-in-progress elements, not finished acts: the megacut plan references renders/ directly, and no delivery.json key, Prod/ hardlink, README row or CHECKSUMS entry is created for them. When the dinosaur pass lands they can be promoted; until then Prod/ keeps meaning 'a finished act'.
_clean_renders: Every canonical movement is rendered CLEAN -- no fades, no overlays, no cards. Fades live in stories/megacut/megacut.json in act-film time, which is this repo's convention (see megacut.json `_transitions`), and it is also what makes these files editable: the dinosaur pass gets unfaded picture to work on rather than footage with a dip already burned into it. A movement may additionally declare an `ending_derivative` (movements 4 and 5 do): a SEPARATELY NAMED output rebuilt directly from the same original source and audio window by its own builder -- movement 5's carries the underwater passage, and movement 4's composes the movement's OWN REPLACEMENTS and its chat plates in the same single encode, so the swaps and the words never travel in separate encodes. The derivative is never a mutation of the clean render -- the clean file keeps its name, its window and its bit-identical audio, and the derivative adds no x264 generation before megacut assembly because it is encoded once from the source, not from the clean render.
_rights: Third-party copyrighted: Nuclear Blast recording with the accepted third-party 4K picture upload O0lyFqLr3Cc. The full rights record is music/bed_perfume_of_the_timeless.json. The original measured audio stream remains the bed; the re-upload is picture-only and its accepted 'Nightwish. ://: Arena.' watermark remains visible. PROTOTYPE OUTPUT, same as the prologue: the non-commercial shipping presentation embeds rather than re-hosts the media, so these renders are for cutting and review and receive no public social copies.

movements.seat: after act I (01-intro), before act II's slide
movements._in_point: The owner said '~1:31 or wherever the last cut left off'. There are TWO answers and this is the reconciliation. The prologue's PICTURE leaves off at 91.200; its SONG leaves off at 99.200, having faded from 93.000. Resuming at 93.000 replays exactly the 6.2 s the prologue faded DOWN, under a 6.2 s fade UP (applied in the megacut plan), so the song dips out across act I and swells back instead of restarting -- one continuous performance with a hole in it rather than two plays of the same bar. Resuming at 99.200 was the alternative: gapless song, but 8 s of picture silently skipped.
movements._free_match: There is NO shot boundary between 91.200 and 108.960 -- it is one continuous shot. So movement 2 resumes the very shot the prologue left, and the join is invisible by construction rather than by treatment. This is the reason 93.000 costs nothing on the picture side.

flash._what: THE JUMP SCARE. A hard full-frame cut-in of the angry Bluefin raptor, 0.100 s -- about six frames at the delivery rate, long enough to register and too short to read as a shot. Owner 2026-08-17: '4:17 ... the jump scare is too early' / '4:21 put the jump scare here. Analyze the audio for maximum effect' -- so it MOVED from source 140.960 to the largest onset inside the named window, re-measured rather than guessed: librosa onset strength (spectral flux) over the whole shot 138.920-144.520, window 142.983-143.483 (4:21 plus the +/-0.25 s the stamps carry). The window's best onset is 1.603 at source 143.216, replacement-relative 4.296. replacements._source: renders/artwork/roar.png. THE SOURCE IS LOW RESOLUTION AND THAT IS A FINDING, not a choice: the largest published copy of this drawing anywhere is characters/angry.webp at 553x352 (the header/ copy the owner linked is 440x280), and ublue-os/artwork -- where the owner expected a high-quality one -- HAS NO CHARACTER ART AT ALL, only wallpapers. Checked 2026-08-15 across the whole website checkout including its worktrees and dist/. So the flash is a 2.82x upscale, composed in ONE Lanczos step straight to 1920x1080 so the renderer's fit is a no-op and it is never resampled twice. It is six frames of flat vector-style art, which is the only reason this is shippable. A master would be a straight swap: replace renders/artwork/roar.png and re-run scripts/build_interludes.py. _replacements: SHOT REPLACEMENT, added 2026-08-15 on two owner notes about the SAME thing -- putting Project Bluefin's own artwork into the interludes. This is the 'dinosaur pass' these movements were rendered clean FOR (_clean_renders below), arriving one pass earlier than expected. EVERY REPLACEMENT IS DURATION-LOCKED to the shot it covers, measured with `select='gt(scene,...)'` on the source and never rounded, so a movement's length cannot change and no chapter marker downstream can move. The picture is swapped; the SONG IS UNTOUCHED and plays through the replacement, which is what keeps the thread one continuous performance. Art is cached by scripts/fetch_artwork.py from ublue-os/artwork -- this project's own artwork, not a third party's.
_artwork_fidelity: ALL ARTWORK IS CACHED AT ITS PUBLISHED RESOLUTION and resampled exactly ONCE, at render time, straight to the delivery frame. Owner, 2026-08-15: *'I am tired of you defaulting to low rez videos, music, and pictures, this is a HIGH FIDELITY presentation'*. The first pass did the opposite twice over -- it centre-cropped every wallpaper to 16:9 and downscaled it to 1920x1080 at fetch time, then stretched it to 1920x804 at render time to match the film's scope window. That cropped into the drawings AND squashed them. Now: scripts/fetch_artwork.py saves the native file (up to 7680x4320, vectors rasterised at a 3840 long edge on their own aspect), and build_interludes.py fits with force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease and pads the difference. Never stretched, never cropped -- the owner's call on the bars: *'letter box is fine'*.
